issues.legal_issue: A reviewing court cannot treat lower courts as having found that a custom covers leasehold transfers when they found only that the custom was co-extensive with the general law of pre-emption.
material_facts: The trial court found a local custom of pre-emption co-extensive with Mahomedan Law.
The first appellate court endorsed that finding and separately concluded that the particular leasehold property could be pre-empted because its holder was for practical purposes an owner.
The High Court treated the lower courts as having found that the custom itself extended to transfers of leasehold property.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was wrong to attribute to the lower courts a finding that the custom applied to leasehold transfers; their finding was only that the custom was co-extensive with Mahomedan Law.
issues.legal_principle: The scope of a finding about a custom must be determined from what the lower courts actually found. A finding that a custom is co-extensive with Mahomedan Law does not itself establish that the custom applies to a category of property excluded by that law.

predicates.second_appeal_from_preemption_decree: A party brought a second appeal from a decree in a pre-emption suit.
predicates.lower_courts_found_only_general_custom: The lower courts found that a local pre-emption custom was co-extensive with the general law, without finding that it covered leasehold transfers.
predicates.higher_court_attributed_leasehold_scope_: The higher court stated that the lower courts had found the custom applicable to transfers of leasehold property.

issues.definition: When a second appeal concerns a pre-emption decree, and the lower courts found only a general custom but the higher court attributed leasehold scope to that finding, the higher court has misread the lower-court findings.

issues.legal_issue: A custom of pre-emption co-extensive with Mahomedan Law does not permit pre-emption of a leasehold interest.
material_facts: The property sought to be pre-empted was parjoti land, meaning a permanent leasehold interest.
The proved local custom was co-extensive with Mahomedan Law.
The claim was based on rights of vicinage and participation in appendages.
issues.conclusion: The leasehold property could not be pre-empted under the custom, whatever the ground on which the pre-emption claim was made.
issues.legal_principle: Mahomedan Law of pre-emption requires full ownership in the property transferred; it does not apply to the sale of a leasehold interest. The pre-emptor must also have full ownership, because reciprocity is the basis of the right. The Court relied on Mulla, Principles of Mahomedan Law (15th ed.), Baboo Ram Golam Singh v. Nursing Sahoy, Phul Mohammad Khan v. Quazi Kutubuddin, Dashrathlal Chhaganlal v. Bai Dhondubai, Rameshwar Lal Marwari v. Pandit Ramdeo, and Oudh Behari Singh v. Gajadhar Jaipuriya. It distinguished Bhagwati Prasad v. Balgobind because that case concerned a claim under a different law, not Mahomedan Law.

predicates.preemption_suit: A claimant brought a proceeding seeking to pre-empt a transfer of property.
predicates.custom_coextensive_with_general_muslim_l: The proved local pre-emption custom extended no further than the general Muslim law of pre-emption.
predicates.transferred_interest_is_leasehold: The interest transferred was a leasehold interest rather than full ownership.

issues.definition: In a pre-emption suit, when the proved custom is co-extensive with general Muslim law and the transferred interest is leasehold, that interest is not pre-emptible under the custom.
